must_remember: The reciprocal of the equivalent focal length of thin lenses in intimate contact is the algebraic sum of the reciprocals of individual focal lengths: $1/F = 1/f_1 + 1/f_2$.
Total power of lenses in contact is given by the algebraic sum of individual powers: $P = P_1 + P_2$.
When two thin lenses are separated by a distance $d$, the equivalent focal length formula becomes $1/F = 1/f_1 + 1/f_2 - d/(f_1 f_2)$.
The total linear magnification for lenses in contact is the product of individual magnifications: $m = m_1 \times m_2$.
Optical power is measured in dioptres ($D$) when the focal length is expressed in meters.

glossary.meaning: The focal length of a single hypothetical lens that produces the same optical effect as a combination of lenses.
The degree of convergence or divergence of light rays, defined as the reciprocal of focal length in meters ($P = 1/f$).
The distance along the common principal axis between two coaxial thin lenses.
A combination of two lenses designed to eliminate or reduce chromatic aberration.
